Abstract › Results (11 AIP studies, 724; 4 CIP studies, 1872); Table 1 arm sizes as listed; editors' sums recomputed: trials 514, AIP studies 724, CIP 1872. Five trials of 25 to 28 days, then 6, 8 and 12 weeks (Results › Amphetamine-induced psychosis studies, 2nd paragraph). The six head-to-head trials match card sc_srisurapanont_2021.

Results › Methodological quality has four running-text paragraphs (figure captions not counted): 1st (five low, Wang 2016 dropout 12/42, Leelahanaj and Samiei high), 3rd (Coffin and Sulaiman 2011 fair), 4th (Herbst poor).

Measures of effect; Table 2. Recomputed by the stated formula with equal n: Wang 2020 3.402 and 3.459, Verachai 3.594 and 3.836, Wang 2016 3.423 and 4.024, Sulaiman 2011 1.942. Between-group p values as listed.

Primary outcomes › Amphetamine-induced psychosis, 3rd paragraph; Table 2 Farnia row (between-group p < 0.001 for SAPS, 0.08 for SANS, read in the page structure; footnote a: end values are mean differences from baseline).

Every number matches Table 2 (footnotes c and d), Table 3 2a-2 (retention 48.74 vs 43.08 days, p 0.023; lost to follow-up 11 vs 22, OR 0.31) and the 3rd and 4th paragraphs. The note's 'both trials enrolled people with low symptom levels' is right for Wang 2019 (baseline PANSS 37.8 and 36.2) but not from this review for Sulaiman 2013: Hall gives no baseline for it and its Table 1 threshold is the presence of psychotic symptoms. The low level comes from the network meta-analysis (card sc_srisurapanont_2021, PANSS 51.6), and the note should say so. The reference-list title of Wang 2019 ('after acute treatment') supports reading it as a continuation trial.

key_findings.correction: d = 0.951 is the within-arm fall in craving on paliperidone (the placebo arm's within-arm d is 0.761), not a between-group effect; the between-group comparison is p = 0.03 (Wang 2019, Table 3 2c), and for aripiprazole p = 0.015 on the BSCS with no effect size (Sulaiman 2013). The review's text presents 0.951 as superiority over placebo, and the finding repeats that. The urine result (52.6% to 42.9% vs 55.6% to 43.8%, no significant difference) is right, and the review says two studies had objective measures, one of them an RCT.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 and low confidence (one critical flaw, item 7) are right on the reading the project applies. One question for the senior author changes the overall if read strictly. The review restricts eligibility to peer-reviewed literature without a reason (and then includes a dissertation). AMSTAR 2's partial yes on item 4 needs any publication restriction to be justified, so the logic of senior decision 21 (an unjustified language limit is 'no') would make item 4 'no' here too. That would add a second critical flaw and make the overall critically low. The project has no precedent for a publication-status restriction; the cards so far count a missing grey-literature search only against 'yes'.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial rather than minor. The card's own four gaps are right, but the main one sits in the abstract's conclusion, the sentence most readers see: it says the review 'found support for the effectiveness of antipsychotic drugs'. That rests on within-arm changes from baseline, labelled 'huge' in the results, which cannot separate drug from recovery with time and abstinence, plus two small placebo-controlled trials in stabilised or already-improving people. The cautious Conclusion section (a clear conclusion cannot be drawn) does not reach the abstract. The project rated a comparable abstract-level overstatement substantial (Boden 2023, senior decision 23).

missed: Key finding 5 and the cannot_establish and interpretation fields say both placebo-controlled trials enrolled people with low symptom levels. This review shows that only for Wang 2019; for Sulaiman 2013 it gives no baseline, and the low level comes from the network meta-analysis's figure (PANSS 51.6), which the card should cite.

Wang 2019 craving (Table 3 2c): the d of 0.951 is within-arm, yet the text presents it as superiority over placebo. The printed paliperidone baseline SD of 0.08 is probably 0.8: the printed d values are approached only with SD 0.8 and end-point numbers of 29 and 18 (40 minus those lost to follow-up), giving 0.949 and 0.761 against the printed 0.951 and 0.761. This also suggests that the review's formula used the end-point n here (editors' calculation).

Table 3 2a-1 gives Wang 2016 a between-group p = 0.01 on the Simpson–Angus Scale (aripiprazole 0.1 to 3.4, risperidone 0.2 to 3). Fluyau 2019 reports no significant difference between the drugs on that scale, so the reviews disagree on this trial's side effects.

Demographics field: Table 1 gives Sulaiman 2013's diagnosis as amphetamine dependence (DSM-IV/5), with methamphetamine use and psychotic symptoms as the threshold. So five trials, not six, are labelled as methamphetamine psychosis or dependence, and three are labelled by amphetamine.
Minor: the Ongoing substance use paragraph gives paliperidone 27%–75% of the BNF maximum; Table 1 gives 25%–75%.
